summary.en: Security forces continue search operations in Jammu and Kashmir's Poonch and Mendhar districts while a 29-year-old woman was injured in a bear attack in the region. In Manipur, 84 BSF personnel were hospitalised with food poisoning after a morning meal and a Kuki-Zo woman was killed and her husband wounded in an ambush by suspected Naga militants in Kamjong, leaving two civilians missing. Leaders of the Cockroach movement remain jailed for violating a protest-site ban and protesters are bypassing internet blackouts with Bluetooth. 437 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Sikkerhetsstyrker fortsetter søkeoperasjoner i Jammu og Kasjmir sine distrikter Poonch og Mendhar, mens en 29‑år gammel kvinne ble skadet i et bjørneangrep i regionen. I Manipur ble 84 BSF-personell innlagt med matforgiftning etter et morgenmåltid, og en Kuki-Zo-kvinne ble drept og hennes ektemann såret i et bakholdsangrep av mistenkte Naga-militanter i Kamjong, noe som etterlot to sivile savnet. Ledere av Cockroach-bevegelsen sitter fortsatt i fengsel for brudd på forbudet mot proteststed, og demonstranter omgår internett-nedstengninger med Bluetooth. 437 kamprelaterte dødsfall i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Kashmir conflict
background.extract: The Kashmir conflict is a territorial conflict over the Kashmir region, primarily between India and Pakistan, and also between China and India in the northeastern portion of the region. The conflict started after the partition of India in 1947 as both India and Pakistan claimed the entirety of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. It is a dispute over the region that escalated into three wars between India and Pakistan and several other armed skirmishes. India controls approximately 55% of the land area of the region that includes Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, most of Ladakh, the Siachen Glacier, and 70% of its population; Pakistan controls approximately 30% of the land area that includes Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan; and China controls the remaining 15% of the land area that includes the Aksai Chin region, the mostly uninhabited Trans-Karakoram Tract, and part of the Demchok sector.
